steps.note: S4.1.6 states the net target change (JV+RG)x is independent of the initial scratch values a,c because rows 0-1 subtract exactly the old contribution (and the last rows restore them, S4.1.5); matches the paper.
S4.1.7 gives the bit-case central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, side injection cancelling intersection one, intersections zero/two already zero, self coefficient one, net y <- y+x.
S4.1.8 gives complex central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2, side wires cancelling intersections zero and two, intersection one contributing zero, self coefficient one.
S4.1.9 gives the three stages (x,y) -> (x,y+x) -> (-y,y+x) -> (-y,x) with every invocation restoring its own scratch wires.

The plan only says S4.3.4 'tabulates the orthogonal residual of every edge' and gives the gate-label-by-time table (S4.3.4.1); the per-edge residuals and dimensions (the residual table) are not stated except the two edges 2->5 and 3->4 in other steps, so it names the table without its content.
S4.3.4.2 states t_X perp t_Y gives <t_X> inside t_Y-perp, nested labels, residual P tensor <t_X,t_Y>-perp of dimension h-2.
S4.3.4.3 says the only decreasing edge is centre 3->4 losing h (L = Ich); S4.3.4.4 gives telescoping at each gate, sources N, sinks Wm-N, signed Wm-2N, absolute adds 2L.

S4.3.4.5 asserts residuals are nondegenerate and nonalternating (norm-one vector) and 'hence has an orthonormal basis', but gives no construction of the basis, in particular nothing about splitting off unit lines and absorbing alternating planes; it asserts the result without the sub-step's mechanism (unsure, so absent).
S4.3.5 states L_b/N = 100/539 and L_c/N = 101/539 (also in S4.3).

S4.3.7.3 gives wt(z+w) = wt(z)+wt(w)-2|supp cap supp| with even intersection for z.w=0 so weight is additive mod 4; S4.3.7.4 gives q_V - q_U = sum over an orthonormal basis of wt(v)[v.x] mod 4, negated on decreasing edges.
wt(v) odd because v has norm one (S4.3.7.4); S4.3.7.5 writes i^(eps[v.x]) as (1+i^eps)/2 + (1-i^eps)/2 (-1)^(v.x) and uses H diag(1,-1) H = X to get the kernel aI+bX_v or its inverse.

S4.3.7 has one kernel per residual basis vector with total count s_c and S4.3.7.7 has C^(mk) on k columns; the tensor-over-columns statement (one factor (C^eps) tensored f times per residual basis vector, s_c in all) is made explicitly only in S4.6.1.4 and S4.6.1.7 in the butterfly-layer setting, so this is a looser match.

S4.3.7.6 gives C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a), Z_{a,k} before and i^(27k) Z_{a,k} after, via C = iZC^{-1}Z; S4.3.7.7 gives negating the X outputs so every role carries C^(mk); the plan never states explicitly that the zero label has frame I and the full label C^(m), a minor omission.
S4.3.5 says both L/N ratios are below 1/2 so a strict saving remains; S4.3.6.2 and S4.3.7.2 give s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b < W_b m and the complex deficit 2N - 2L_c > 0.
S4.4.1 defines eta = (Wm-s)/(Wm) and gives 339/22587335000000 for the bit network, matching the paper.
S4.4.1 gives eta_c = 73/19906842167500 for the complex network, matching the paper.
Both deficits exceed 20*2^-50 (S4.4.1), log m < 20 from m < 2^20 (S4.4.2), m^(1-2^-50) > m(1-20*2^-50) > m(1-eta) (S4.4.3), hence s/W < m^tau with tau = sigma = 1-2^-50 (S4.4.4).

S4.5.1.2 gives the pivot at the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, clearing left and below by lower-triangular elementary matrices, scaling, deleting the row and column and repeating; S4.5.1.1 and 4.5.1.2 give Pi with exactly a ones (pivots = rank).
S4.5.1.3 states a fixed odd prime avoiding all denominators and diagonal numerators in a finite table of factors so rational identities specialize to Z/q^b with invertible triangular factors.
S4.5.1.4 states a lower triangular transformation costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order.
S4.5.1.5 gives D_j <- D_j+H_i, interchange (H_i,D_j), D_j <- H_i-D_j taking (h,d) to (h+d,d) with one interchange per one, a in all.
S4.6.4.1 and S4.6.4.2 give E = 64(W+m+1)^3, B = s+E, nu = min{j>=1: m^j >= B}, C_1 = max{20, nu+3}, C_0 = 128 m B^2, Delta = ceil(C_0 d^C_1), with nu = 11 and C_1 = 20 here.
S4.6.4.3-4 count gates and operations per invocation (24W^3+4s+4W+4 < E since s < Wm) and S4.6.4.5 states A(e) <= sA(e/m)+E at an internal node and A(e) <= 8e at a leaf, noting it uses s not s/W.
S4.6.4.6 gives at most ceil(log_m d) levels, sx+E <= Bx, B^(k+1) <= B^2 d^nu, A(e) <= 8dB^(k+1) <= 8B^2 d^(nu+1); S4.6.4.7 totals below 128 m B^2 d^(nu+3) <= C_0 d^C_1.
S4.6.4.8 gives depth-l values in 2^-(p+l) Z[i] with modulus at most 2^l, so p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits are exact; S4.6.4.9 gives epsilon*C_1 < 1 so Delta = o(p).

S4.6.5.6 states every row of H has absolute row sum one so disk arrays map to disk arrays, truncation cannot increase either component and errs by less than 2^-p each, so total error is below sqrt2 * 2^-p.

summary: 24 of 26 present, 2 absent (L1, L4), none wrong. The plan carries the bank-exchange proof, the nested-label budget (side edge, decreasing edge, telescoping, loss ratios), the phase interface (weight additivity, kernels, endpoint repair), the rank-saving arithmetic, the matrix-shear lemma and the simultaneous-layer depth/precision bounds. L1: no per-edge residual table. L4: asserts an orthonormal basis without the absorb-alternating-planes construction. P3 matches only loosely, through the layer-setting steps S4.6.1.4/S4.6.1.7; P4 omits the explicit statement that the zero label has frame I and the full label C^(m).
